title: The Mural Palette
clue: A handful of paint chips and a street with something to say.
reveal: Collect free paint-chip cards and take them on a stroll past murals and street art. Match each color to a wall, and your dog chooses the last color by where they stop.
objective: Walk a quiet route of murals and public art with four paint chips, find a match for each, and let your dog pick the fifth.
instructions: Pick up four or five paint-chip cards from a hardware store (they are free), or cut colored paper scraps. Add one blank card. Keep them all in a pocket or small tote bag; they never go near your dog's mouth.
Choose a quiet route with murals or public art, ideally a weekday morning with little traffic. Pavement walking only, with pausing space beside each piece.
Set off on a loose leash with water and waste bags. Let your dog sniff as you go; the walk is not a race.

At each mural, stand a little back from the wall, doors and seating. Take a chip from your tote, hold it up at chest height away from your dog, and look for its match or near match. Tick it off, then put the chip back in the tote.

The Dog's Chip: let your dog pick a spot between murals and sniff there for as long as they like. When they move on, look up and find the nearest color, pick the closest chip from the tote (or note it on the blank card) and announce 'the dog's color' with a flourish.
Keep your dog off the wall, off any wet paint and out of doorways. The chips stay in your pocket or tote the whole walk.

At the end, sit on a bench with your dog beside you and lay the chips in a row on your far side, out of reach, with the dog's chip last. Take one photo of the palette, then put the chips away. At home, stick them to a sheet as your palette poster.
twist: A paint-chip palette turns a street walk into a color hunt, and the final color is chosen not by you but by wherever your dog stops longest.
variations: Sculpture version (shapes instead of colors): at public art in a park, hunt for a circle, a triangle, a wave and a spiral in each piece.
Seated version: pick one mural beside a bench or plaza, match the chips from your seat, and let your dog sniff the pavement near you.
Quiet version: choose a weekday morning on a side street, or a mural court away from traffic.
No-art version: match the chips to colors in a neighborhood garden or a block of doors.
completion: You have matched your chips to colors around you and added a fifth chosen by your dog, then made your palette.
photoIdea: The paint-chip palette on a bench with your dog's nose, paw or leash beside it.
memoryPrompt: Which color did your dog choose, and where did they stop?
supplies: Paint-chip cards or colored paper scraps
A small tote bag or pocket
substitutes: Colored paper, wrapping paper or fabric scraps instead of paint chips
safety: Stay on the pavement, away from traffic, doorways and seating; keep your dog on a short leash near roads.
Keep your dog off walls and wet paint; chips stay in your pocket or tote, never within chewing reach.
Carry water and rest in shade; skip hot days and end the walk if it gets crowded.
